name: Mass casualty and triage
description: Triage tags, patient lists, Medical Branch worksheets, treatment areas, the transportation log and hospital calls for a mass casualty incident, with the structured decisions a Medical Group makes: declare an MCI, name the triage method, assign a destination and close a hospital to arrivals. Stays at the coordination and decision level; it is not a patient simulator and not clinical guidance for a real incident.
outsideParties: the receiving hospitals and the regional healthcare coalition

advisorRoles.name: Triage Unit Leader
advisorRoles.description: Applies the triage method, keeps the tag count, and sends patients on to treatment areas by priority.

advisorRoles.name: Treatment Unit Leader
advisorRoles.description: Runs the treatment areas by priority (Immediate, Delayed, Minor), the morgue or holding area, and the supplies and staff the areas need.

advisorRoles.name: Medical Communications Coordinator
advisorRoles.description: Calls the hospitals for capability and capacity, relays destination decisions and keeps the hospital status board.

advisorRoles.name: Air Ambulance Coordinator
advisorRoles.description: Owns landing zones, air medical requests and the destinations air units can reach.

decisionForms.label: Declare a mass casualty incident
decisionForms.description: The incident commander or the first Medical Group Supervisor declares an MCI, which starts the regional plan.

decisionForms.label: Set the triage method
decisionForms.description: The Medical Group names the method every crew uses, so tags mean the same thing.

decisionForms.label: Assign a patient to a destination
decisionForms.description: Send a tagged patient to a hospital by a stated mode, with the reason.

decisionForms.label: Open or close a hospital to arrivals
decisionForms.description: Record a hospital's status change as the Medical Communications Coordinator learns it, or a decision to stop sending patients there.

decisionForms.label: Issue a public statement
decisionForms.description: The PIO releases a casualty count, a hospital notice or a reunification instruction.

glossary.definition: Mass casualty incident: more patients than the first resources can treat and transport, so the Medical Group runs patient flow.

Walkers are Minor. Breathing over 30 a minute, capillary refill over 2 seconds (or no radial pulse) or not following commands make a patient Immediate; no breathing after the airway is opened is Expectant or Deceased; the rest are Delayed.
Sort, Assess, Lifesaving interventions, Treatment and/or transport. A global sort, then individual assessment with quick lifesaving interventions; categories include Expectant and Dead.
Pediatric version of START; child vital signs differ from an adult's.
Immediate (red), Delayed (yellow), Minor (green), Expectant (black). Always print the word, never color alone.
Survival unlikely with the resources available. Still comforted and reassessed, not abandoned.
Runs triage, treatment, transportation and medical communications; titles (Branch or Group, Director or Supervisor) vary by jurisdiction.
A hospital asks ambulances to go elsewhere because it cannot take more patients of a kind.

productConventions: Triage tag: unique number, priority word, the vitals the named method uses, injuries in plain words, time and who triaged. Patients are fictional and unnamed: age and sex only.
Patient list: one row per tag. Transport log: time, tag, priority, unit, ground or air, destination, why. Counts agree across every product.
Hospital call record: hospital status (Open, Limited intake, Diversion, Closed), beds by category, patients assigned. An offer is a promise the transport log respects.
Times are 24-hour. Reunification notices reuse reunification_notice and press_release.
realismRules: Say which triage method the players use (START, SALT or the local method); no federal rule picks one.
Patients are fictional; never use real names or a real incident's patient list.
Immediate patients leave first, to a hospital that can treat the injury (trauma, burn, pediatric), not only the nearest.
Expectant patients are reassessed and comforted, never left without a person.
Children get a pediatric method and a hospital with pediatric capability.
No hospital gets more than it said it could take; capacity changes during the incident and the log shows it.
Tag count, patient list, transport log and the PIO's number agree unless an inject says why not.
MCI is declared before treatment areas open; no transport leaves without a tag; ambulances arrive in a trickle.
Stay at who decides what; no clinical procedures, doses or treatment steps.
